speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I quote verbatim: "I have been a witness to a suicide, I have lost a friend to suicide and I struggle with suicidal ideation on a near daily basis.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: It cost me my university education, landed me in tens of thousands of dollars in debt, and left me with little means to earn enough to pay back my study loan and survive on my own.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I will likely never be able to earn more than $1,000 per month and will likely take my life than die of other causes in the near future." Other than Lucy, there were 46 more people who came forward to share with me about their experiences with suicide, among the 400 respondents to the public consultation on mental health conducted by my team and I.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Like Lucy's and the many near and far ones who have reached out to me, each and every one of their stories was heartbreaking to know and read, as they agonised over their struggles to live.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Sadly, so did the number of elderly aged 60 and above who took their own lives.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: From 2017 to 2019, there were 1,204 attempted suicides yearly.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Last year, the Immigration and Customs Authority reported that there were 8.36 suicides per 100,000 Singapore residents in 2018, up from 7.74 in 2017.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Suicide has entrenched itself as the leading cause of death for those aged 10 to 29.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: According to the Attorney-General's Chambers, a classification of "suicide" only occurs when there is clear evidence of suicidal intent and self-harm.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: From my interactions with suicide-bereaved parents, the cause of death is sometimes categorised as "fall from a high place" or "unnatural death" and also labelled as such on the requests of family.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, we must also not forget that for every suicide and attempted suicide we know, there are many more people struggling with self harm and suicide ideation that we have little data on.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How have we managed to develop from a third-world to first-world country and yet not be able to successfully tackle this issue of suicide?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How is it that we still have the current number of suicide deaths we have today?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: One large reason might be the disappointing fact that Singapore was not listed as one of the few "high income" countries with a national suicide prevention strategy even though we are a member state of WHO – because we do not have one!

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: National suicide prevention strategies are essential for working towards the ultimate goal of suicide reduction.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: According to WHO, such a strategy is important as it indicates a government's clear commitment to prioritising and tackling suicide, while making resources available for necessary interventions.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Building on this, I hope to use the rest of this speech to ask the Government to go further in developing a national response that aims for zero suicides under this review as part of a multi-ministry and multi-sectoral effort.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But first, let me take this opportunity to address the discourses about suicide.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: It is a common fear that talking about suicide could encourage suicide behaviour, hence many friends and families who are concerned about their loved ones in distress often struggle with asking about suicide ideation or intent.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, Minister Ong Ye Kung shared his concerns in this House that talking about suicide numbers in schools "may heighten suicide risk in vulnerable youths".

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: While I appreciate the intention of these concerns, I would like to point out that youths today already consume a large volume of media online related to mental health and suicide.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Youths have shared with me that schools often try to keep quiet about students who died due to suicide, but this backfires as students are often already in the know about their peers' mental health and suicidal intention.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The expert consensus is that, to have a chance at preventing suicide, we must talk about suicide responsibly.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Earlier this month, Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong indicated that allowing for treatment for self-inflicted injuries in MediSave or MediShield Life could encourage suicidal behaviours, although exceptions could be made for those with existing mental health conditions.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In this House, a few colleagues expressed their concerns last year that decriminalisation of suicide could send the wrong signal in incentivising suicide.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: These views perpetuate the stigma by shrouding suicide in exclusion.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Experts indicate that incentives for help-seeking are helpful in combating stigma, allowing those who are struggling to feel more comfortable in seeking support.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Intense feelings of hopelessness can also arise from sudden and adverse life events including unemployment, trauma and the loss of loved ones.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Not every suicide is a result of mental illness, nor is someone with mental illness always suicidal.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Lastly, we must take the lead in recognising that suicide is far from a selfish choice and cannot be blamed on the individual.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: My cousin, who has attempted suicide several times, often shares that he feels that he's a burden to his family, including me, even as he acknowledged that he knows how much we love him.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Studies have shown that people who attempt to take or took their own lives commonly feel that their lives hamper others, viewing their decisions as relieving their loved ones.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The following excerpt of a suicide letter from an elderly victim broke my heart, I quote: "Father is reluctant to leave all of you.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: One example would be to expand funding for organisations like SOS, the Samaritans of Singapore, not just to operate our de-facto national suicide helpline, but to ensure timely follow-ups with callers who need further support.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, studies show that 83% of people who die by suicide visit some kind of doctor a year before their death.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, healthcare facilities, especially emergency facilities and departments, are a logical place to prevent suicides.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: By getting our hospitals to track suicide attempts, our national strategy is better placed to coordinate the continuity of care for these suicide attempters.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: In the mould of the Zero Suicide Initiative, we must ensure that on the individual level, that we acknowledge each person's pain, empower them to make safe decisions and on the systems level, build hope for recovery with a continuity of care approach across agencies.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We should also note that since the decriminalisation of suicides, data of suicide attempts is no longer required by the Criminal Code.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Without data surveillance of attempted suicides, our ability in developing informed strategies is limited.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Through a national strategy of data surveillance coordinated across Government agencies and community partners, the transparency and awareness of the support available can be improved, allowing various stakeholders better position their role and plan their work in tackling suicides.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: They believe there needs to be clear and strong suicide prevention and post-suicide intervention protocols in schools.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Despite their inconsolable grief, they came forward to share what they believe could be done to prevent more teen suicides so that other parents do not have to go through the same pain.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Families and friends, especially other students in the school, will inevitably suffer from grief and trauma to varying degrees and urgently need this post-suicide intervention support.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Many education systems such as the state government of Victoria in Australia establish step-by-step guidelines on what to do in the event of a suicide attempt and/or in an occurrence of suicide, making them publicly available as part of a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Notwithstanding the peer support networks that Minister Indranee cited in response to my question in Committee of Supply (COS) on MOE's suicide prevention strategy, I am sure we all agree that laying out clearly MOE's suicide protocols to parents and students can only help confront increasing suicides amongst teens.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Studies show that 50% to 60% of all persons who died by suicide gave some warning of their intentions to a friend or family member.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Movement shared she was not aware that her 11-year-old son was suicidal until it was too late.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Young people have often asked me what the warning signs are and how they can help their friends.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We need more public education programmes in schools, workplaces and communities on suicide prevention 101, including learning these warning signs: from unusual and sustained changes in actions, to actions like withdrawal, loss of interest, words like verbal statements such as "Everybody will better off without me", "What is the point of living?", and feelings – guilt, hopelessness; also, biological and physical aspects like poor sleep and loss of appetite.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Key gatekeepers like police, teachers, grassroots leaders and more must also be trained in suicide first-responder training so that they can intervene appropriately for suicide attempts.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Community support groups like the SOS as the first community responder, or the PleaseStay.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Movement and new groups like Caring for Life are key stakeholders in this whole-of-society effort to reduce and prevent suicides.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: However, without a national strategy for these efforts to align to, we risk having a fragmented and sub-optimal approach to supporting survivors and bereaved parents.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We must stand firm in the belief that suicides are preventable and commit to the efforts in making that possible.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Because unlike any other targets – like 2020 for gender equality, 30 by 30 for food security – that we have made in this House when it comes to loss of lives; human lives, nothing short of zero has ever been good enough for us.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: A Zero-Suicide Singapore as a goal joins the Vision Zero aspiration of our workplace safety and health policies and the Zero Accident movement in our public transportation policies too.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The United States aspires towards a nation free of the tragedy of suicide in its national prevention strategy.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Japan envisions a society where no one is driven to take their own life.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: To Lucy and those of you who are struggling with suicidal thoughts out there, please know this: "You are not a burden nor are you alone.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, the world will be a better place in it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is also lower than the annual global age-standardised suicide rate of 10.5 per 100,000 population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The number of elderly suicides has declined from 126 cases in 2014 to 115 cases in 2018 despite an ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that every suicide is one death too many and we have and will continue to strengthen our strategies to prevent suicides, as guided by the National Mental Health Blueprint and Community Mental Health Masterplan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Through partnering Ministries and agencies, we have adopted a multi-prong approach to suicide prevention based on the following key strategies of building mental resilience; encouraging help seeking and early identification; supporting at-risk groups; and providing crisis support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have also invested in resources for mental health as well as put in place monitoring and tracking mechanisms to evaluate the effectiveness of our programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As noted by Ms Ong, there are social and environmental factors that contribute to the individual's intent to self-harm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Therefore, our strategy targets upstream protective factors in addition to strengthening downstream supportive services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Suicide prevention and intervention strategies have been developed in schools, workplaces and in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As part of suicide prevention strategy, MOE has focused on upstream efforts to build students’ social and emotional skills and resilience through the school curriculum, CCAs and various programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) also offers mental well-being programmes to equip students with the skills to cope with stress, overwhelming emotions, interpersonal conflicts, change and transitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At the workplace, HPB conducts mental well-being roadshows and workshops to provide stress management tips and techniques to employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MOM’s Workplace Safety and Health Institute, in partnership with other agencies have developed an assessment tool, iWorkHealth, as well as a website to help workers identify workplace stressors and resources to improve one’s mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the National Seniors’ Health Programme, HPB organises healthy ageing workshops that include psycho-social education modules aimed at empowering our seniors aged 50 years and above with the knowledge and skills to manage their mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Early identification and encouraging help seeking are vital for suicide prevention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, we have invested in raising mental health literacy through training and education programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond SOPs, school teachers are trained to identify students experiencing distress, provide timely support and refer students in distress to school counsellors or mental health professionals for further interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Peer support structures are also being established in schools and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) by HPB as well as MOE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Community Health Assessment Team (CHAT) offers easy access to mental health resources and help via different avenues for young persons between 16 and 30 years old.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Young persons may either visit the CHAT hub, log onto CHAT’s online portal for its WebCHAT service or call CHAT’s hotline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) conducts programmes on how to identify suicide warning signs and where to seek help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Agency of Integrated Care (AIC) has been working with community-based organisations to set up Community Outreach Teams to reach out to seniors with or who may be at risk of dementia or depression.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Anti-stigma efforts play an important role in encouraging persons in distress to seek help early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Hence, in 2018, the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) rolled out a multi-year public education campaign, called "Beyond the Label" to achieve this objective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NCSS also recently launched the Beyond the Label Helpbot, Belle to make access to mental health information and resources to the community easier for the general public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We recognise that persons who are greatly distressed and attempt to take their own life requires help and the criminal justice system may not be the best option.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, the Government will continue to track reports of such cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Additionally, public hospitals are working on tracking attempted suicide cases that they attend to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There are a range of services in place to support at-risk groups of all ages in our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, we have trained Silver Generation Ambassadors to identify seniors who live alone, and to proactively offer them befriending services, identify and escalate cases with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We also have services in place to support persons in distress who require assistance such as Institute of Mental Health (IMH)’s 24-hour mental health helpline and the SOS' hotline which is funded by NCSS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I agree with Ms Anthea Ong that every life matters, and we will continue to strengthen our efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: During this year’s COS, MOE shared that they will feature mental health education in the revised Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) and MOH will also be setting up an Integrated Youth Service (IYS) in Woodlands this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have established platforms for a coordinated interagency approach to suicide prevention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, the Inter-Agency Research Workgroup for Youth Suicides, brings together agencies to study the issues surrounding youth suicides and to facilitate deeper collaboration between the various agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The workgroup will be sharing their recommendations, for agencies to follow up later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This Network brings people together to identify opportunities and gaps to work on, to improve youth mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There is no easy solution to suicide prevention as the causes are complex and multifaceted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even as we undertake a whole-of-Government review to enhance our efforts, a whole-of-society approach is necessary to build mental resilience in order to prevent suicide in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: COVID-19 for instance poses yet another huge test for all of us, not least in mental resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond the Government’s resources and support as well as the many community programmes and efforts, I urge my fellow Singaporeans to stand together, look out for each other, develop strong empathy and reach out your hand to others to uplift them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Only together, can we ensure each other's mental well-being, especially in such unprecedented times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On this note, let me conclude by thanking the Member for her selfless efforts to promote mental well-being and prevent suicides.
